confidence_notes: Restaurant and coffee anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living figures returned in my web searches. Numbeo, as summarised in the results, gave about 142.5 SEK for an inexpensive meal, 850 SEK for a mid-range meal for two, 48 SEK for a cappuccino and 70 SEK for a domestic draft pint. Wise and Hikersbay gave similar USD figures: about $15 for an inexpensive meal, about $92 for a mid-range meal for two, $4.70-5.12 for a cappuccino and $7.56 for a half-litre of draught beer. I converted SEK to USD at about 9.6 SEK per USD, a rate inferred from the USD and SEK pairs these sources gave. I did not search for this rate. Cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. They come from a nightlife guide's ranges, not from aggregated indexes: about 140-175 SEK for a cocktail and 95-130 SEK for a glass of wine. These are consistent with Swedish bar prices being roughly 2x and 1.5x the beer price. Accommodation anchors are model estimates for the July 2026 summer peak, based on general knowledge, with no live booking or listing checks. The FX observation is the AUD/USD rate at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026 as reported in the search results, which attributed it to the RBA exchange-rates page. I did not open that page directly. The figures used are an RBA-attributed value plus aggregator and guide data. Sources: numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Gothenburg; wise.com/us/cost-of-living/sweden/gothenburg; hikersbay.com/prices/sweden/gothenburg; eurocityguide.com/sweden/gothenburg-nightlife-guide; rba.gov.au/exchange-rates-overview.html.
comparable_city_reasoning: Gothenburg is Sweden's second city. In the Numbeo comparison returned by my searches, its restaurant prices were generally lower than Stockholm's and its cappuccino price was nearly the same. For accommodation I used Stockholm and other Nordic second cities, such as Bergen and Aarhus, as the basis, with July being high season.
